slot.brief: Assign R/S configuration to a molecule drawn as a Fischer projection.

stem:
The absolute configuration of the chiral centers in the following Fischer projection is:
$$
\begin{array}{c}
\text{COOH} \\
| \\
\text{H}-\text{C}_2-\text{OH} \\
| \\
\text{HO}-\text{C}_3-\text{H} \\
| \\
\text{CH}_3
\end{array}
$$

verdicts.working: Compound is 2,3-dihydroxybutanoic acid. C2 priorities: OH > COOH [C(O,O,O)] > C3 [C(O,C,H)] > H. In Fischer, horizontal bonds point toward viewer; H is horizontal at C2, so reverse apparent rotation: OH(right)→COOH(up)→C3(down) appears CCW (S) → actual R. C3 priorities: OH > C2 [C(O,C,H)] > CH3 > H; H horizontal again: OH(left)→C2(up)→CH3(down) appears CW (R) → actual S. Verified by signed-volume (determinant) calculation with Fischer 3D geometry: C2 = R, C3 = S.

working:
1. Configuration at $\text{C}_2$:
- Assign CIP priorities to the four groups attached to $\text{C}_2$:
  1: $-\text{OH}$ ($Z = 8$)
  2: $-\text{COOH}$ (carbon bonded to $(\text{O}, \text{O}, \text{O})$)
  3: $-\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ ($\text{C}_3$, carbon bonded to $(\text{O}, \text{C}, \text{H})$)
  4: $-\text{H}$ ($Z = 1$)
  Since $(\text{O}, \text{O}, \text{O}) > (\text{O}, \text{C}, \text{H})$, priority order is: $-\text{OH} > -\text{COOH} > \text{C}_3 > -\text{H}$.
- On the Fischer projection, $-\text{OH}$ is on the right, $-\text{COOH}$ is at the top, and $\text{C}_3$ is at the bottom.
- Tracing $1 \to 2 \to 3$ gives a counter-clockwise path.
- Since the lowest priority group ($-\text{H}$) is on a horizontal bond, the apparent configuration is reversed: counter-clockwise corresponds to $R$.
- Thus, the configuration at $\text{C}_2$ is $2R$.

2. Configuration at $\text{C}_3$:
- Assign CIP priorities to the four groups attached to $\text{C}_3$:
  1: $-\text{OH}$ ($Z = 8$)
  2: $-\text{CH(OH)COOH}$ ($\text{C}_2$, carbon bonded to $(\text{O}, \text{C}, \text{H})$)
  3: $-\text{CH}_3$ (carbon bonded to $(\text{H}, \text{H}, \text{H})$)
  4: $-\text{H}$ ($Z = 1$)
  Priority order is: $-\text{OH} > \text{C}_2 > -\text{CH}_3 > -\text{H}$.
- On the Fischer projection, $-\text{OH}$ is on the left, $\text{C}_2$ is at the top, and $-\text{CH}_3$ is at the bottom.
- Tracing $1 \to 2 \to 3$ gives a clockwise path.
- Since the lowest priority group ($-\text{H}$) is on a horizontal bond, the apparent configuration is reversed: clockwise corresponds to $S$.
- Thus, the configuration at $\text{C}_3$ is $3S$.

Combining both centers gives $(2R, 3S)$.
